title: The Mezz Mezzrow record with Benny Carter and mixed bands in New York
summary: Duerr recalls his Brunswick record with Mezzrow, Benny Carter, Teddy Wilson and Floyd O'Brien, and whether mixed bands played clubs.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well of course you never knew that rock and roll was that? No. Did you ever know Mez Mezroy around here?

Yeah, I got a record I made with him. Oh yeah? Yeah. I got the record here. The only record I got was an old Brunswick record. And I played it some time ago but I don't know if it got wonk, it don't sound so good no more.
Teddy Wilson was on it. Was he any good then? Yeah, he played fine.
When he first came to New York, he was one of his first, I guess one of his first record dates. I got the record here. I like to hear a good machine sometime but I think-

Well, we'll, we have to come and get all this stuff together and we can all go over there. Tulane and maybe we can weight the needle down or something and we might take that. Yeah, I think so might take it, yeah.
You want to try it sometime? Yeah. You want to do it any time you want.
Yeah, well you dig all the stuff out and then we'll come. Well, that's, yeah I'd like, see I'd like to make a tape of that. Who else was on the record with you with Maz?
I'm trying to think now. Maz and Benny Carter was on it, I know that.
What was he playing then?
He played sax but he played trumpet on the last chorus I believe.
Was he playing good trumpet then or was he?

Well he played pretty good. I didn't know Benny too well. I made a date with him but I didn't know him. I heard of him a lot too around New York. He was well known even then. You know what I mean? And I'm trying to think who was on trombone. Was that Floyd O'Brien on trombone? I'm trying to think.
I'm pretty sure.

Yeah, Floyd O'Brien is who played trombone. I always get that record mixed up with the ones I made with Wingy because it was a mixed band. They both were mixed bands. I was playing and I'd get them mixed up sometimes. Yeah, Floyd O'Brien made that record.
Was that many mixed bands playing around New York or just recording sessions?

Well they made records together. But did they play in clubs? I played a radio broadcast with Chick Webb one time, at the radio station with Chick Webb, the short punch back drum, you know, stand up and play. He played a mess of drums, boy.
But what about in the clubs? Did they have clubs that used mixed bands?

Not in the clubs so much, no, they didn't use mixed bands in the club, or the ballrooms. Now like I said, there was in the ballroom that had colored bands, they had white bands, but they had some good, like Louis Russell's band and some other colored bands at that time, Louis Russell and oh I can't think of it, Kenny Scott and Pippenow, some others, I can't think of it. Did you know the guys in Louis Russell's band? No, I didn't get them all. About half of them from New Orleans, you know? Well they were, but I didn't get the, I wasn't that long of a band. I used to go up and hit a band, but I didn't know them enough, you know, to get to know them, you know?
Did you know, what did Maher's play like is what I'm trying to say?

Oh I can't, he played pretty good, but I can't remember the styles of them, so I've got to listen to the record myself to bring back the memory, I really can't tell. What about Pop Foster, was he any good? Well that's what Pop Foster made the record with, let's see, yeah with Mez, yeah he was on the record day, Pop Foster that's right.
Yeah and he was with Louis Russell too, you know, and Nong. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.

That's right, I mean, I. That's right. I mean, I. That's right. That's right. Eddie Wilson. Who, did they do, did you have arrangements in the band? Yeah, there was, somebody made arrangements for me. I don't know who he was, maybe, you know. I wish the dumb machine was kind of a fit for him.
